Injection 4 already achieved the maximum CRF; shorten its gradient while holding the solvent window and temperature fixed to seek a faster fully resolved method. Its minimum resolution of 3.52 provides substantial margin for gradient compression.

Shorten the gradient another grid step while keeping temperature and solvent endpoints fixed. Injection 9 retained ample resolution (minimum R 2.88), so this should further reduce analysis time while preserving the maximum CRF.

Test the next shorter gradient with solvent endpoints and temperature unchanged. The minimum resolution of 2.44 leaves room for further compression, potentially preserving CRF 1.000 with an even earlier last peak.

Raise temperature one grid step to shorten the fastest fully resolved method while keeping gradient steepness unchanged. Monitor the first pair closely: its R of 1.86 leaves only modest margin above the full-credit threshold.

Test the minimum gradient duration while lowering temperature to strengthen separation of the critical early pair, whose resolution improved at lower temperature. This explores a faster fully resolved method without pushing the marginal 45 C separation further.

Raise the final organic fraction one step to accelerate the last peak, which eluted during the hold in injection 13. Keep the low temperature to protect early-pair selectivity, while checking whether the slightly steeper gradient preserves its marginal R of 1.61.

Lowering phi0 worsened early-pair resolution, so test one step above the fastest fully resolved method instead. The narrower gradient window may improve the critical pair while slightly advancing the last peak.

Increase phi0 one more step to test whether narrowing the gradient window continues to improve early-pair resolution and shorten elution. Monitor the first pair for loss of retention, since excessively high starting organic fractions caused co-elution in earlier runs.

Raise temperature one step to shorten the fastest fully resolved method while keeping the gradient fixed. The early pair's R of 1.77 provides modest headroom, but its temperature sensitivity makes it the key limit to check.

Test whether one further increase in starting organic fraction can shorten elution while retaining full resolution. This probes the upper solvent-window boundary: the first peak is already near the unretained region, so early-pair compression is the main risk.

Return to the resolved starting fraction and test one temperature step above injection 18 to establish the speed limit. The early pair may fall below R 1.5 given its temperature trend; injection 18 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Back off to 30 C and slightly reduce the final organic fraction to improve the critical early pair through a shallower gradient. This targets more resolution margin than injection 18 while retaining a very short run and maximum CRF.

Lower temperature to improve the critical early-pair margin while retaining the minimum gradient duration. Since maximum CRF is already secured, this tests a slightly slower but potentially more robust alternative to injection 18.

Test a lower starting fraction around the robust two-minute method to keep the first peak farther from the unretained region. Neighboring runs suggest full resolution should be retained with only a small time increase; injection 18 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Raise temperature one step from injection 23 to shorten this fully resolved alternative while checking the early pair's remaining margin. This refines the local temperature boundary without repeating a method; injection 18 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF result.
